items.title: Why Chalmers's budget will rein in the property free-for-all
items.description: After being rejected twice by an electorate that didn't want to give up lucrative tax arrangements on property, the Albanese government has sniffed the breeze and decided the time is ripe for change.

items.title: The Australians the treasurer has in mind as he targets home ownership
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers will hand down the federal budget tonight. It's expected to tackle housing inequity, but will it bring back the Great Australian Dream?

items.title: What will be in tonight's federal budget? Here are the major measures we know about so far
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is unveiling his fifth budget tonight, and housing for younger Australians will be a centrepiece.

items.title: Live: Smaller deficits forecast as Chalmers prepares to hand down fifth budget
items.description: The federal budget will remain in the red over the next four years, but the deficits will be smaller than those forecast six months ago. Follow live.

items.title: More or less quiz: Follow the money and see what it gets you
items.description: A new quiz format? In this economy? Celebrate budget day with our More or Less challenge.

items.title: 70 MPs call on Starmer to quit despite bid to reset leadership
items.description: The British prime minister is fighting to fend off a growing threat to his leadership after a disastrous set of local election results last week.

items.title: 'Didn't have the balls': Hume takes shot at Labor after shocking Coalition loss
items.description: Deputy Liberal leader Jane Hume is promising a new day for a Coalition that has lost its way, but whether the party can recover from the wreckage of Farrer remains to be seen.

items.title: Trump, Xi and the AI race that could reshape global power
items.description: When Trump last visited China in 2017, artificial intelligence was not yet the centre of global power. Now it is.

items.title: Delta 'proud' to be at Eurovision as five nations boycott competition
items.description: This week, the Eurovision Song Contest will burst onto the stage in Vienna, and onto screens around the globe, but behind the colour and campness, this year's competition is shaping up as one of the most politically charged in history.

items.title: Relief but no justice after discovery of body believed to be triple murderer
items.description: A family member of one of the victims of the Lake Cargelligo shootings says justice has not been served despite the discovery of a body believed to be that of Julian Ingram.

items.title: No link between PCOS and higher rate of abnormal cysts: study
items.description: Despite what the name suggests, women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) do not have a higher rate of abnormal ovarian cysts than the general population, a large study shows.

items.title: New study links residential air pollution to hospital admissions
items.description: A new study has found a clear link between air pollution exposure and the risk of ending up in hospital. It's a battle Julia Ovens knows only too well.

items.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire on 'life support', with energy woes to continue
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he's aiming for "complete victory" in Iran as the US and Iran reach an impasse in negotiations.

items.title: Cricket Australia hoping private owners can make BBL a cricket 'grand slam'
items.description: Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg says private investment in the Big Bash League is "inevitable" and waiting for too long could mean "we've missed the boat" as more competitions pop up around the world.

items.title: The caring burden for childless daughters
items.description: Single women over 45 without children are much more likely to be spending time caring for family members who are aging, have a disability or chronic illness. And it's not just costing them financially.

items.title: Inside the US blockbuster that brought $68 million to the Gold Coast
items.description: The $110 million Mortal Kombat sequel is the next in a laundry list of productions putting Queensland on the radar for international films.

items.title: Indulgent breakfast recipes to enjoy at home
items.description: From shakshuka to French toast, you can enjoy an indulgent breakfast or brunch at home with one of these recipes.

items.title: The university where teaching is tougher than having terminal cancer for this academic
items.description: The University of Newcastle has been found to be worst in class when it comes to staff wellbeing. Now, an academic with terminal cancer is speaking out about it because others fear they cannot.

items.title: Vanuatu drops limitations on China in key pact with Australia
items.description: The ABC can reveal that after months of difficult negotiations, the Nakamal Agreement has been approved by Vanuatu's cabinet but omits key limitations on China's influence.

items.title: Apple's Tim Cook and Tesla's Elon Musk among top US CEOs to accompany Trump to China
items.description: According to a list shared by a White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, Elon Musk and Tim Cook will be accompanied by 15 other chief executive officers when Donald Trump visits China.

items.title: Small robots drafted to help tackle looming renewable skills shortage
items.description: Students are using tiny, programmable robots to code in a bid to encourage them to consider careers in renewable energy due to predicted skill shortages.

items.title: High Court to hear challenge over murder verdict swapped to manslaughter
items.description: The case of a Canberra man convicted over the death of his partner after she fell from the bonnet of his car will reach the High Court today, after the ACT Court of Appeal swapped the jury's verdict of murder to manslaughter.

items.title: Window for smelter offers closes, with worker torment over jobs continuing
items.description: The window for non-binding offers to purchase for the Liberty Bell Bay smelter, in Tasmania's north, has officially closed, with a union delegation taking their cause to Canberra as workers anxiously await news.

items.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship passengers to quarantine in Perth
items.description: Australian passengers who were on board the hantavirus-hit cruise ship will be ordered to quarantine in Perth for at least three weeks.

items.title: Felicity's been waiting for a house as long as Tasmania's housing agency has existed
items.description: Felicity Hirst says she is not too picky about what kind of house she lives in; she just wants one. She has been on Tasmania's social housing list for three and a half years — as long as the state's housing authority has existed.
